A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EnerVerse work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and included appendices support comparison, with content matchable across renaming, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: V2 reports original RT-1 video-generation evaluations, LIBERO policy experiments and ablations, and real-world block-placement results in Appendix A.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds CALVIN evaluation, domain-adaptation and texture-shift experiments, and a quantitative 4DGS hallucination study.

M1.justification: The chunk-wise diffusion framework, sparse memory, geometry-conditioned multi-view generation, 4DGS loop, and policy head using first-denoising-step features are retained. V3 expands their specification and replaces FAV terminology, without establishing an actual procedural or architectural redesign.

E1.justification: V3 adds CALVIN evaluation, LIBERO scenarios with unseen floor and container textures, a cloth-folding generation example, and reported fruit-sorting experiments. The original RT-1, LIBERO, and pretraining coverage remains; Isaac Sim was already used in v2, so its expanded dataset description is not a newly added dataset.

E2.justification: V3 adds RoboFlamingo, GR-1, 3D Diffuser, and SUSIE as CALVIN comparators in Table 3. It also adds OpenVLA to the real-world block-placement comparison in Table 7. The original RT-1 and LIBERO baseline methods remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include CALVIN's ABC-to-D five-subtask evaluation without memory resets, pooled training across LIBERO suites, and a 50-episode data-engine evaluation by two blinded experts. Table 2 additionally evaluates RGB plus one rendered view and MAIL with two static RGB inputs.

E4.justification: V3 adds a generation-adaptation ablation in Table 8, texture-shift and pooled-training analyses in Appendix E, and a controlled comparison with and without 4DGS in Appendix I. It also adds qualitative generation failure cases. The original sparse-memory and training-strategy ablations remain, while the existing attention analysis moves to Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds for LIBERO and five block-placement trials per compartment. V3 introduces no changed repetition counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing practices. The additional expert-rater count describes the new evaluation protocol.

E6.justification: Table 2 corrects MAIL's average from 83.5 to 81.2 while retaining its per-suite scores, and adds an 85.5 average for RGB plus one rendered view. New results include CALVIN average sequence length 3.00, policy scores of 93.2 versus 85 without generation adaptation, texture-shift results, and 40% fewer hallucinations with 4DGS. Original RT-1 and retained EnerVerse LIBERO scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The underlying diffusion mathematics is retained. V3 spells out the existing v-prediction parameterization and formalizes the already-described action-diffusion head, but introduces no substantive mathematical revision, new theoretical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: V3 reframes the claimed novel FAV contribution around a multi-view generative prior benefiting single-camera deployment. Its abstract also adds an efficiency claim of about 280 ms per eight-step action chunk. The central claims about sparse-memory diffusion, the 4DGS data engine, and robotic policy performance remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive discussion of video quality versus control success, domain-gap-induced generation failure, CALVIN's memory-transition difficulty, and interpretations of rendered-view gains. It also discusses OpenVLA's instruction-following advantage and explicitly identifies limitations involving artifacts, heuristic camera poses, and understanding how generation supports policy learning.

D1.justification: Appendices F-H and Table 10 substantially expand training hyperparameters, dataset statistics, action-head specifications, GPU budgets, memory use, and latency information. Camera conditioning, feature caching, and data-engine implementation are also clarified. These are mainly new disclosures; some specifications remain inconsistent, including 14 DiT blocks in Figure 12 versus 18 in Appendix G.

R1.justification: V3 adds Gen3C discussion, explicit ray-conditioning and Scene Representation Transformer references, and citations supporting the CALVIN comparisons and next-best-view limitation. AgiBot World and Pulsar citations are removed. The broader positioning against video-pretraining and 4D-generation research remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, and multi-view/action-method descriptions, and replaces FAV terminology. Related work moves after the experiments, attention analysis moves into the appendix, and the appendix organization expands from A to A-I. These constitute extensive narrative and structural revision.

P2.justification: V3 combines v2 Figures 2 and 3 into a composite Figure 2, revises the rendered-view illustration, and relocates attention maps. Comparison tables gain rows, and new CALVIN, adaptation, robustness, and hyperparameter tables appear alongside new qualitative and architectural figures. Typography, page layout, and display placement are extensively revised.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens validation through CALVIN, adaptation and texture controls, a real-world comparator, and a direct 4DGS ablation where v2 offered limited supporting evidence. It also corrects MAIL's average and supplies substantial training and computational details. These gains address important validation and documentation gaps, outweighing remaining implementation ambiguities such as the conflicting DiT block counts.
